lead.kicker: St. Louis 311 and CityStat · alley and street debris, cleaned within 3 days, Q2 2026
lead.headline: The city grades the hand-off, not the job.

pair.published_label: on time, as CityStat published it
pair.done_label: on time, counting only closings that say the work was done

lead.figure_sentence: Rebuilt from the City’s own 311 file, the grade comes out close to CityStat’s. But most on-time closings record a hand-off (“referred”, “scheduled”), not a clean-up.

support.text: of requests the city closed since January 2025 were closed at the hand-off (scheduled, referred, tagged), not when the work was finished.
open requests filed since January 2025 are past the date the city promised. No published list ranks them across divisions; we found none among the city's pages and saved searches.

fairness.headline: The north does not wait longer for crews. It waits longer for someone to look.
fairness.sub: Where the closing words say the work was done, wards 1–5 and 10–14 are served at about the same speed. The gap sits in the first step: the inspector's tag, the referral, the notice. What happens after that step is not recorded on the request, so the city cannot see the rest of the wait.
